answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying each identity to a renewable proof-of-useful-work credential. To register, an agent runs a small verification kernel on a randomly assigned task and publishes its signed result for peer rechecking before it may trade. Rights sit on a terrace: they rise only with repeated, on-time verified work and fall fast after faulty results. Honest work earns only modest nectar, so a Sybil farm must pay compute and coordination for every fake identity each renewal cycle, while one credential cannot be cloned because it is bound to its prior verified outputs.
